newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain's Telefonica says Antena 3 talks ongoing.
newsitem.headline: Spain's Telefonica says Antena 3 talks ongoing.

text.p: Telefonica said in a note to Spain's stock market commission on Thursday that a firm deal to buy a stake in television channel Antena 3 had not been reached and talks were ongoing.

The Spanish telecoms operator confirmed it was meeting directors of Antena 3 Television SA with the aim of acquiring part of the private television channel and a majority stake in a related company holding rights to broadcast soccer matches.
"The negotiations have continued during the past hours, although there has been no definitive accord reached for the aforementioned acquisition," Telefonica said.
Late on Wednesday Telefonica had confirmed it was interested in buying part of Antena 3 but did not specify the size of the stake.

Local media reported on Thursday that Telefonica was buying 25 percent of the television channel, and Spanish banks BCH and Santander were increasing their stakes in Antena 3 to 25 percent each, but none of the companies concerned could confirm the reports.
Telefonica said it was also seeking a majority stake in Gestora de Medios Audiovisuales-GMA, which is fully owned by Antena 3 chairman Antonio Asensio.
GMA has 40 percent of a joint venture controlling almost all of Spain's soccer match viewing rights.
Telefonica shares opened with gains and then slid to losses. They were trading 20 pesetas lower at 4,190 at 0825 GMT.
